title: Coordinated Reservation (Gang) and Latency Fencing for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Priya Srinivasan
description: This PRD proposes a coordinated reservation ("gang") mechanism and a complementary latency-fencing policy to improve tail latency guarantees for multi-request workflows on Dedicated capacity. The feature targets workloads that need multiple concurrent GPUs or tightly coupled inference requests (e.g., multi-shard models, ensemble pipelines, batched chat sessions) and suffer from high P95/P99 spikes due to partial allocation or noisy neighbors.
problem_statement: Certain customer workloads require simultaneous allocation of multiple GPUs or concurrent slots to meet end-to-end latency SLOs. Current reserved-pool allocation on Dedicated can assign capacity incrementally which leads to partial placement, head-of-line blocking, and cascading tail latency. There is no first-class support for atomic group allocation or temporary latency fencing to prevent noisy neighbors from violating SLOs during surges.
goals: Allow customers to reserve and atomically acquire groups of slots (gang reservations) to support multi-shard and ensemble workloads
Provide a latency-fencing policy that enforces stricter co-location or isolation rules during an ongoing request to preserve tail latency SLOs
Integrate with existing reserved pools and autoscaling so gang allocations respect tenant quotas, burst budgets, and pre-warm heuristics
Expose metrics and runtime traces in Console to diagnose gang failures, partial allocations, and fence evictions
non_goals: Replace multi-tenant billing primitives — pricing/charging changes will be out of scope for initial launch
Implement custom scheduler from scratch — reuse runtime scheduling primitives and cluster allocator where possible
Support arbitrary cross-region gang allocations in v1
success_metrics: Reduce P99 tail latency for multi-shard workloads by >= 40% on average in controlled benchmarks
Decrease frequency of partial-placement errors for gang-enabled tenants to < 2% of allocation attempts
Less than 5% increase in cluster fragmentation compared to baseline (measured over 7-day rolling window)
Telemetry: adoption by at least 10 Dedicated customers in first quarter after launch
assumptions: Runtime already exposes atomic allocation hooks (allocate_all_or_none) or can be extended with limited changes
Most multi-shard tenants can declare the required gang size up-front in their route or model config
Pre-warm/predictive heuristics will reduce cold allocation failures; gang requests will be eligible for pre-warm where possible
proposed_design: High-level flow: 1) API/Config: extend Dedicated reservation spec with optional 'gang_size' and 'latency_fence' boolean fields; 2) Placement: cluster allocator attempts an all-or-nothing acquisition across required nodes or capacity slots, with configurable timeouts and backoff; 3) Fencing: if 'latency_fence' is true, runtime applies temporary QoS isolation (preferential scheduling, CPU/GPU QoS cgroup limits, or tenant-weight bump) for the duration of the request and a short cool-down; 4) Fallback: on allocation failure within timeout, system can either queue request, fail fast, or fall back to a lower-guarantee variant per tenant policy; 5) Telemetry and Console: surface allocation trace, fence events, and recommended actions. Implementation will reuse reserved-pool accounting and autoscaler signals.
technical_requirements: API: reservation schema extension and SDK bindings (JS/Python/Go)
Allocator: allocate_all_or_none primitive with bounded wait and cancellation
Runtime: ephemeral tenant QoS adjustments implementable via scheduler weights or cgroups
Console: dashboard tiles for gang allocation success rate, fence evictions, and fragment impact
SLOs: define time-to-acquire thresholds and labeling for requests that used gang allocation
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal alpha): implement allocator primitive and unit tests; Phase 1 (private beta): enable for 3 internal customers with large ensembles and an opt-in console toggle; Phase 2 (public beta): broader availability to Dedicated tenants with doc-runbook; Phase 3 (general availability): SLA-backed offering with default guardrails and recommended limits. Rollout includes feature flag gating, canary percentage, and migration scripts for existing reservations that specify gang_size=1.
acceptance_criteria: API: customers can create/update reservations with gang_size and latency_fence flags via REST/SDK
Allocator: gang allocations succeed atomically or fail cleanly within a configurable timeout
Fallback: documented fallback behaviors (queue/fail/fallback-model) available and tested
Observability: Console surfaces gang allocation latency histogram and a 'fence_evictions' count; runtime traces link allocation events to tenant and request IDs
Performance: controlled benchmark demonstrates >=40% P99 improvement for representative multi-shard workload compared to baseline
Safety: cluster fragmentation measured and documented; fragmentation increase must remain below 5% in test harness
open_questions: What default timeout should we use for gang allocations? (30s vs 60s vs 120s)
Which QoS primitive provides the lowest-risk isolation across cloud providers (scheduler weight vs cgroup limits vs GPU MIG partitioning)?
How should pricing/units be represented for fractional temporary QoS increases or reserved gangs?
Should gangs be pre-emptible or eligible for opportunistic capacity when underutilized?
timeline: Apr 2026: runtime QoS integration and internal alpha
Jun 2026: public beta and observability polish
Jul 2026: GA if stability criteria met
notes: This PRD is intentionally conservative on cluster-level changes: prefer small allocator extensions and ephemeral QoS experiments over a full scheduler rewrite. We will measure fragmentation and iterate on backfill heuristics as usage grows.
